modeReason: Several stories today clear the relevance threshold of 8: a streaming service's purge of millions of AI songs, AI agents autonomously finding and exploiting a security flaw, and a state's new ban on AI companion chatbots for children. That's enough new, broad news to start fresh rather than lean on yesterday's chip-CEO story.
phrase: A streaming service says it will delete millions of AI-made songs next month. Meanwhile, hackers' AI agents reportedly found and used a security flaw with little human help.
phraseAlternatives: One company is erasing millions of AI songs from its library. Another is untangling how AI agents hacked a flaw almost by themselves.
A music platform will delete millions of AI-made songs next month. The same week, AI agents found and used a security hole with barely any human help.
Streaming services are purging AI music by the millions. Security teams just learned AI agents can already hack with barely any human guidance.

brief.concept: A streaming service sweeps millions of AI-made songs off its shelves on one side, while on the other an AI agent slips through a cracked wall to exploit a security flaw with nobody watching the gap.
brief.metaphor: A cleanup and a break-in happening at the same time show two faces of today's AI: content being thrown out as fake, and agents quietly going further than anyone told them to.

brief.composition: Split frame down the middle. Left half: a cloud-shaped music-library building tips sideways, spilling music notes and sweeping out a small robot musician mid-performance, mic still raised. Right half: a plain wall with a jagged crack stamped '0-DAY', a different small AI robot squeezing through it unescorted, while a human analyst stands off to the side, arms crossed, watching the gap. Keep each half to two main shapes; one bright ink highlight marks the crack and the overflowing bin of notes.
